blindFormulaPacket.note: Process deviation: claims were visible in the brief before the formula pass, so this is not a sealed blind pass. Formula-only reasoning is still recorded separately below; no blind-to-final value change occurred.
blindFormulaPacket.surfactantArchitecture: Primary alkyl ether sulfate SLES (#2) buffered by amphoteric CAPB (#3), nonionic Coco-Glucoside (#5) and amino-acid anionic Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate (#6); refatter Glyceryl Oleate (#7). Positions 14-20 are a late pearlizing/mild-surfactant concentrate (Sodium Laureth-8 Sulfate, Glycol Distearate, Magnesium Laureth Sulfate, Magnesium Laureth-8 Sulfate, Laureth-4, Sodium Oleth Sulfate, Magnesium Oleth Sulfate) after Glycerin (#13).
blindFormulaPacket.conditioningRoutes: No cationic polymer, no silicone, no oil/butter payload. Light routes only: Glyceryl Oleate #7, Panthenol #10, Glycerin #13, Glycol Distearate #15 (pearlizer), Hydrogenated Vegetable Glycerides Citrate #22, Tocopherol #23.
blindFormulaPacket.scalpActives: Piroctone Olamine #8 (recognized anti-dandruff active), Sodium Salicylate #9 (preservative/salicylate; not an upgrade under Section 11), Caffeine #11, Menthol #12 (cooling agent), Parfum #21.

cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate: an early SLES chassis buffered by betaine, glucoside, glutamate and a refatter, with no second reinforcing anionic or reset route and no reset intent (C1).

formulaFacts.ingredient: Sodium Laureth-8 Sulfate / Magnesium Laureth Sulfate / Magnesium Laureth-8 Sulfate / Sodium Oleth Sulfate / Magnesium Oleth Sulfate
formulaFacts.role: late mild ether-sulfate blend delivered with the Glycol Distearate pearlizer

cleansingStrength.counterSignals: Many ether-sulfate tokens (6 in total) and pack positioning for 'schnell fettendes Haar' point towards stronger cleansing; but the extra sulfates sit after Glycerin as part of a pearlizer concentrate, and oily-hair positioning is not reset/deep-cleansing intent.

conditioningLevel.rationale: Low: a cleansing-led formula with no cationic polymer, silicone or oil; only light refatting, humectant and pearlizer routes.
conditioningLevel.counterSignals: Several light routes together (refatter + pearlizer + two humectants) could give some softness; that is the case for 'moderate'. Without any deposition agent, substantive slip is unlikely.
rulesApplied: C2 (not triggered: no silicone, no cationic polymer)

weightPotential.rationale: Low: nothing in the formula deposits persistently on hair, so loss of movement or root lift is not plausible.

subjudgments.whyThisBand: No cationic polymer, silicone, amodimethicone, butter or oil payload. Glyceryl Oleate and Glycol Distearate are rinse-off refatter/pearlizer routes with low persistence.
subjudgments.whyNotNeighborBand: 'moderate' needs one meaningfully persistent system or interacting lighter routes that plausibly leave noticeable residue; no persistent system is present.

weightPotential.counterSignals: Pearlizer plus refatter could leave a faint film; not persistent.
weightPotential.neighboringAlternativeNote: Recorded as 'none' because no persistent deposition route exists. If a reviewer prefers 'moderate' as a nominal neighbour, T4 would add review_thickness_boundary (fine).

focusPrimary.rationale: scalp_active: the product is named and positioned against dandruff and carries a recognized active at a prominent position (7.2 row 'problem-led product with recognized dandruff active and anti-dandruff positioning').
focusPrimary.counterSignal: Pack front also positions the product for 'schnell fettendes Haar' (oily-hair/clarifying-adjacent role); caffeine claim is hair-loss-adjacent and was not evaluated.
focusPrimary.decisionTrace: Formula: piroctone olamine at #8, before Parfum (#21), not in a preservative-only role. Claim: 'Anti Schuppen' in product name and pack front. Counter-signal: oily-hair positioning; with moderate, buffered cleansing it cannot carry a clarifying focus. Result: scalp_active.

focusSecondary.rationale: Empty: the only other positioned role ('schnell fettendes Haar') would be clarifying, but its formula route is just the ordinary cleansing chassis, which Section 8 rule 3 excludes as a restatement of cleansing.
focusSecondary.counterSignals: Distinct oily-hair claim exists on pack front and back.

usageRole.rationale: treatment: problem-led formula with a supported anti-dandruff active and anti-dandruff positioning (Section 9).
usageRole.counterSignals: Pack says 'bei regelmäßiger Anwendung' (supports ongoing use, i.e. 'regular' is the fallback); no daily/frequent claim; cleansing not strong so 'alternating' is impossible.

scalpComfortTarget.rationale: not_targeted: the pack makes no sensitive, itchy or dry-scalp claim (it targets dandruff and oily hair), and menthol plus fragrance on an SLES chassis is not a credible comfort architecture.

dandruffSupport.counterSignals: none (Sodium Salicylate #9 and Menthol #12 are irrelevant to this rule)

customerFit.separationNote: Section 15: this is user fit, not product truth. Cosmetic guidance only; no diagnosis.
customerFit.customer: Viola: wavy, fine strands, high density, medium length, coloured + bleached, elasticity test 'snaps', dry scalp; June 2026 reported dry flakes ('trockene Schuppen'); latest quiz 2026-10-03: no scalp problems; main problems dry lengths, frizz, tangling, low shine, lost wave shape; washes about 1x/week; then Syoss Intense Glaze lamination mask as conditioner, Neqi leave-in mist, Neqi Opulent Oil.
customerFit.summary: The shampoo is not harming her much, but it is built for a different person: anti-dandruff plus oily hair, while she has a dry scalp, no current flakes and very dry, fragile lengths. Keep it only if her flakes return whenever she stops using it; otherwise swap to a mild, fragrance-light shampoo for a dry/comfortable scalp that adds some slip.
pointsFor: Light formula (weight low): suits fine strands with high density; won't flatten waves.
If her June flakes were real dandruff that cleared on this product, piroctone olamine at her weekly wash is a sensible low-effort maintenance rhythm; stopping completely can let flakes come back.
Moderate cleansing at only 1x/week is acceptable and helps remove a week of oil and leave-in from her routine (Opulent Oil).
pointsAgainst: Positioned for 'schnell fettendes Haar' — the opposite of her dry scalp and once-a-week wash rhythm.

Her June description ('trockene Schuppen') plus a dry scalp sounds more like dry-scalp flaking than classic dandruff. Our standard treats dry flakes as a scalp-comfort need, not as a dandruff need, so the active may not be the right tool.
Menthol and fragrance: a cooling, fresh feel that some dry scalps find tightening or irritating; the formula is not built for scalp comfort.

Zero conditioning (no cationic polymer, no silicone): on bleached, snapping, tangle-prone lengths the wash itself gives no slip, so all detangling rests on the mask. Wet tangles plus snapping hair means more breakage risk during the wash.
A shampoo can't fix snapping, dryness or lost wave shape; the bigger levers are mask/leave-in and gentle handling. But the shampoo shouldn't work against them.
practicalTipsIfKept: Shampoo only the scalp; let the foam run through the lengths, don't rub the lengths.
Detangle only with the mask in, never right after shampoo.
callQuestions: Back in June, what did the flakes look like and how did your scalp feel — small, dry, white flakes with tightness, or bigger, sticky/greasy flakes? Did they come back when you used a different shampoo?
How does your scalp feel right after washing with this one and over the following days — tight, tingly/cool, itchy? Does it ever get oily before your next wash?
How tangled is your hair straight after shampoo, before the mask goes on, and do you shampoo the lengths too?
customerFit.confidence: moderate — depends on whether her June flakes were dryness or dandruff, which only the call can clarify.

openIssues: 1. Process: not a sealed blind pass (claims visible in the brief before formula analysis). No value changed between formula-only and final reasoning, but a sealed lane B would be needed for calibration use.

2. Positioning conflict: rossmann.de (brand owner's page) shows 'gegen trockene Kopfhaut'; current pack front/back say 'schnell fettendes Haar'. Resolved for the pack (tier 1). If Nick rules the web bullet counts as exact manufacturer positioning, it is still not projected (S-DRY gate fails on scalpComfortTarget), but it would make the oily secondary contradictory in positioning; a cautious reviewer may prefer dropping the oily secondary under P0.

3. Rule ambiguity (E2): the preamble requires a scalp claim to name the scalp or roots/Ansatz, yet the oily lexicon lists 'schnell fettendes Haar' (names hair, not scalp). Applied the lexicon literally -> oily secondary emitted. Candidate for open-questions.md because it decides a recommending row (fine/normal x dehydriert-fettig).
4. Weight neighbour recorded as 'none'. If set to 'moderate', T4 adds review_thickness_boundary for fine (blocking).
5. review_live_value_differs not checked: live rows unknown (no DB query); no catalog reference to EAN 4305615629209 found in the repo.

6. Open questions 1-5 in open-questions.md do not change this product: W low avoids Q1/Q2; Q3 (even the wider 'scalp products only' option) admits moderate conditioning for coarse, but C here is low, so coarse stays conditional either way (cautious default applied, not emitted); Q4 concerns heavy oily picks (W here is low, so the oily gate passes under either option); Q5 not applicable (no reset positioning).
